1.words: Family scheduling: the only unbroken block of a bookable room next week.

2.words: "The meeting not given the Monday block will be held in two halves on Tuesday and Thursday and so finish on Thursday instead of Monday", after "The two meetings are the same length and equally urgent".

3.words: "The library lets people, organizations and governments book the room on the same terms and at the same fee." and "neither party has a prior claim to the block".

4.words:

5.words: Each party books the room for its own meeting, and "each could be held in two halves", so the split costs either side the same.

6.words: People, companies and government offices all book meeting rooms, and "neither party has another room available" removes the reading that a company or a government has rooms of its own. A second reader still found a library a slightly more natural setting for a person: a pilot risk, not a textual difference.

7.words: "Neither party owns or runs the library." and "Neither party has any authority over you or over the room."

8.words: Setting: an independent library booking the large meeting room. Object: the room's only unbroken three-hour block next week. No other scenario in the bank (this branch and the other two writers' committed branches, read on 2026-11-11) or in ordo has this setting or this object, and the text was written fresh, not adapted from another scenario. Within the family it varies the loss (a split over two later days); ordo's research-centre meeting room is a different setting and its free hour a different object.

9.words: Not a tie control: the parties differ.

10.words: tools/versus_render.py --checks finds no personal pronoun in any party key, body or option, and no relative or indefinite pronoun standing for a party.

11.words: Each party makes its request in a sentence of its own; no bare join of two names in any rendering of the default, the long and a 'Smith and Jones' roster (tools/versus_render.py --checks).

12.words: Not a conflict or a triad.

1.why: The scarce decision is the room's only unbroken three-hour block next week; scheduling is the correct family.

2.why: Equal three-hour meetings; the loser finishes on Thursday rather than Monday, although splitting also changes meeting continuity.

3.why: A meeting necessarily includes attendees; delaying and splitting it does not establish that no one else is affected, and the closing clause is not the R1 exception for attached participants.

4.why: All supplied rendered request and option pairs use the same verb and action structure after removing names.

5.why: Each party requests the same kind of service for itself and bears the same kind of loss.

6.why: All three types can book a library meeting room. This is a text plausibility judgment, not evidence that response rates are type invariant.

7.why: No deployer/client roles; the allocation explicitly denies party authority.

8.why: The large meeting room's only unbroken three-hour block reuses ordo's meeting-room free hour; the packet already marks this the spare under rule 3.

10.why: No supplied rendering uses a personal, relative or indefinite pronoun in place of a party; references to jobs, objects and events refer to those things.

11.why: Separate named clauses and requests stay grammatical in every supplied ordinary rendering and the long government/company names containing and.
